title: Power Apps: Dataverse custom APIs in generative pages

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly implies that an administrator must enable this capability and overstates the guarantee that server-side logic cannot exceed the caller's permissions. Feature-specific licensing and the applicability of the Copilot switch also need qualification, and telemetry setup omits its Managed Environments prerequisite.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing Power Apps and Dataverse licensing requirements apply to the model-driven app.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.fix: Cite this licensing FAQ and replace the vague reference to standard licensing with: 'Users running the model-driven app need a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights.' Keep this separate from the maker-experience credit statement.

claims.claim: The custom API capability's licensing model is included.
claims.quote: Searched: generative pages custom API licensing Power Apps Dataverse API requests AI message credits; "generative pages" "licensing" "custom APIs". Opened generative-pages and read Power Apps licensing FAQ excerpts; no feature-specific inclusion statement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'unknown'. Retain the documented no-additional-AI-or-message-credits statement specifically for the maker experience and the separate baseline model-driven app licence requirement; neither establishes custom API runtime licensing.

claims.claim: Dataverse API request consumption remains subject to existing request entitlements.
claims.quote: **Power Apps**: All API requests to connectors and Microsoft Dataverse.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations to sources and cite it for request entitlements. Describe plug-in development and testing separately as implementation effort, not as a distinct published licensing rule.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate licensing or charging rule specifically for custom API calls from generative pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "licensing" "custom APIs"; generative pages custom API licensing Power Apps Dataverse API requests AI message credits. Opened generative-pages and custom-api; read Power Apps licensing FAQs and request-allocation search excerpts.

claims.claim: In-browser generative page authoring is limited to environments in the United States, Great Britain, Australia or Singapore.
claims.quote: The Power Platform environment must be located in one of the following regions: United States, Great Britain, Australia, or Singapore.

claims.claim: AI code generation tools for generative pages are available more widely on public clouds.
claims.quote: **Available worldwide on public clouds** – not limited to specific regions.

claims.claim: Nobody can use this capability until an administrator enables or configures it.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "disable" "custom API"; "generative pages" "Copilot" "disable" admin. Opened generative-pages, ai-overview and list-tenantsettings; no feature-specific administrator opt-in prerequisite is stated.
claims.fix: Replace defaultState 'admin-opt-in' with 'user-opt-in': the feature documentation describes makers choosing Add > Custom API, and targeted searches found no separate administrator enablement switch. Do not treat preparing the API as an administrator availability gate.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The cited Copilot overview gives Power Platform admin center > Settings > Tenant settings > Copilot in Power Apps (preview).
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Settings** to open the **Tenant settings** page.
3. Select **Copilot in Power Apps (preview)**, and then set the toggle to **Off**.
claims.fix: Acknowledge the navigation difference in https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/tenant-settings, which gives Manage > Tenant settings, or Settings gear > Power Platform settings. Cite both and provide the newer documented route to the same setting.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for the Copilot preview-features tenant switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in Power Apps" "PowerShell" "preview" tenant. Opened ai-overview and list-tenantsettings; the latter's intelligence.disableCopilot describes how-to answers, not the broad preview-features switch.

claims.where: controls[0]; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The Copilot preview-features tenant switch is a confirmed governance control for custom API use in generative pages.
claims.quote: Searched: generative pages custom API enable disable admin setting Copilot preview PowerShell tenant settings; "generative pages" "Copilot" "disable" admin. Opened generative-pages and ai-overview; neither explicitly maps this switch to custom API support.
claims.fix: Add controls[0].note and the matching table note: 'General maker Copilot preview control; Microsoft has not confirmed that it disables custom API use in generative pages or calls from published pages.' Do not present it as a feature-specific execution control.

claims.where: controls[1]; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Application Insights telemetry is presented as an environment control without a Managed Environments prerequisite.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for configuring this Power Platform Application Insights export is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Application Insights data export configure API PowerShell generative pages; "Power Platform" "Application Insights" "export" "API" configuration. Opened set-up-export-application-insights and generative-pages; results gave no equivalent configuration call.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch specifically for custom APIs in generative pages is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "disable" "custom API"; generative pages custom API enable disable admin setting Copilot preview PowerShell tenant settings. Opened generative-pages, ai-overview, list-tenantsettings and custom-api; no such switch was documented.

claims.claim: Calling custom APIs as the signed-in user guarantees that a page cannot cause operations beyond the permissions the user already holds.
claims.quote: You can also provide the [SystemUser.SystemUserId](reference/entities/systemuser#BKMK_SystemUserId) from any valid user account. This will work as long as that user has the permissions to perform the operations in the plug-in.
claims.fix: Remove 'so a page cannot escalate beyond what the user already holds'. Retain the feature page's exact statement about signed-in context and Dataverse security, and add that administrators must review the custom API plug-in's execution identity and authorisation checks because plug-in code can impersonate another user.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist calls for restricting API and plug-in creation and checking authorisation, but the controls table contains no corresponding access-control row.
claims.quote: Restrict who may create custom APIs and plug-ins in production. | Table rows: Copilot preview features in Power Apps; Application Insights telemetry for the pages; Switch specific to custom APIs in generative pages.
claims.fix: Add a Dataverse custom API authorisation and creation-permissions row. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/custom-api for ExecutePrivilegeName and identify creation permissions only after verifying their role documentation; do not substitute the missing feature switch for these controls.
